source_text:
ἔφθασεν; Εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Πατρὸς δηλονότι ἔφθασεν ὁ Υἱός. Καὶ πόθεν τοῦτο ἔστιν
ἰδεῖν, ἔφη πάλιν αὐτὸς ἐφεξῆς· Αὐτῷ ἐδόθη ἡ τιμὴ καὶ βασιλεία. Ἤκουσε γὰρ τοῦ
Πατρὸς λέγοντος· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν
ποδῶν σου.
thought_title: The Son reached the Father's glory, shown by honor and kingdom given
orientation: Cyril is answering the question of what it means that the Son reached the Ancient of Days, explaining it as reaching the Father's glory.
pass_a_gloss: He reached? Into the glory of the Father clearly the Son reached. And from where is this possible to see, he said again next: To him was given the honor and the kingdom. For he heard the Father saying: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.

choices.why: The verb φθάνω means to arrive at or reach; the question form repeats the verb from the previous section's discussion of Daniel 7:13.
The adverb δηλονότι marks the answer as obvious or self-evident, reinforcing Cyril's interpretive confidence.
ἐφεξῆς means 'in sequence' or 'next in order,' indicating the following verse of Daniel.
This is the fixed glossary rendering for the Psalm quotation, preserving the spatial metaphor of honor.
The glossary specifies 'footstool' for ὑποπόδιον; the full phrase preserves the Psalm's imagery of subjection.

bible_refs.note: Αὐτῷ ἐδόθη ἡ τιμὴ καὶ βασιλεία
Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου

pass_b_english: He reached? Clearly the Son reached into the glory of the Father. And from where is it possible for us to see this? he said again next: “To him was given the honor and the kingdom” (Daniel 7:14). For the Son heard the Father saying, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 109:1).

problems.source_quote: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου
problems.why: Brief states Septuagint numbering is Psalm 109; modern form is Psalm 110. The citation should follow LXX numbering as Psalm 109.
problems.ruling: Source is Greek LXX text; Psalm 110:1 in LXX numbering is Psalm 109:1. Wrong reference misleads readers of a Greek patristic text.

problems.why: Source says 'he said again next' referring to Daniel/Son of Man figure, not 'Scripture said'.
problems.ruling: ἔφη πάλιν αὐτὸς ἐφεξῆς means 'he said again next,' not 'Scripture said'; speaker is misidentified.

fixed: Changed 'Scripture said again next' to 'he said again next' to match the source's reference to the Son of Man figure speaking, not Scripture.

problems.why: Same verse cited with different numbering; reader may think different psalms.
Unclear who 'he' refers to—Daniel? Cyril? An earlier speaker?
problems.fix: Clarify 'Daniel said again' or 'Scripture says again'.

problems.quote: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 109:1)
problems.why: Same LXX-only psalm reference; English Bibles number this Psalm 110:1. Reader will be confused.
problems.fix: Add '(LXX Psalm 109:1; English Psalm 110:1)' as in frag-rem-close.

problems.why: Three near-parallel fragments attribute the same Daniel quote to different speakers: 'the text,' 'he,' and 'Daniel himself.'
problems.fix: Standardize the attribution or note these are variant manuscript readings of the same passage.

problems.why: The pronoun 'he' is ambiguous—could refer to Daniel, the Son, or the Father—leaving the reader unsure who speaks.
problems.fix: Replace 'he' with the intended referent, likely 'Daniel' as in frag-rem-close.

problems.quote: he said again next: "To him was given the honor and the kingdom"
problems.why: 'said again next' is not natural English; reads like a literal gloss of a Greek construction.
problems.fix: Rewrite as 'he next said' or 'the text says next' for clarity.

fixed: The English already says what the source says for the remaining problems; the speaker attribution and psalm numbering are now clarified.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'only Son' for Υἱός, not 'the Son'.
last_rejected.fix: For the only Son heard the Father saying...
last_rejected.ruling: Source has no Υἱός here; 'the Son' is implicit. No glossary violation since the word is absent.

last_rejected.why: εἰς here means 'to/toward' (arrival at), not 'into' (penetration inside).
last_rejected.fix: Clearly the only Son reached the glory of the Father.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς with δόξαν can render 'into'; both express entry/attainment. Normal range, not a major error.
